bug_semantics: Authenticated iframe injection in the Web Previews visual inspector. An authenticated user can supply an absolute or scheme-relative external URL in the inspector's `path` query parameter. ContentLinkContext copied that untrusted value directly into `iframeState.path`; UI then put it unchanged into the configured draft-mode endpoint's `redirect` parameter and used that endpoint URL as the iframe `src`. When the draft-mode endpoint follows `redirect`, the iframe leaves the configured frontend and loads the attacker-selected external origin, bypassing the frontend-origin restriction. The advisory states Web Previews <1.0.31 is affected; repository and npm history narrow the actually present visual-editing path to published 1.0.29 and 1.0.30, with 1.0.31 the first fixed release.
flaw_origin: Commit 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 (`Visual Editing`) is the smallest first-writer. It created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx` with `new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search).get('path')` flowing unsanitized into `iframeState.path`, and created `web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx` with `url.searchParams.set('redirect', iframeState.path)` followed by the resulting URL as the iframe source. Later commit 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 only selected among visual-editing frontends and renamed the URL source to `currentVisualEditing`; it did not originate the untrusted redirect sink. The BIC is a preserved single-parent feature-branch commit, not the later normal merge a20d935b50daa9bdde4c88776ace6de5cb65a05d and not a squash aggregate.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672` shows human author and committer `Stefano Verna <s.verna@datocms.com>`, one parent, and the complete message `Visual Editing` with no message body, Co-Authored-By trailer, Generated-with trailer, AI attribution, or bot identity.
evidence: Advisory bundle source `https://api.github.com/advisories/GHSA-X8P2-G6VV-F5MR` identifies CVE-2026-3327 / GHSA-x8p2-g6vv-f5mr, describes authenticated iframe injection and arbitrary-origin loading in Web Previews <1.0.31, and directly references fix 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e. In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S "url.searchParams.set('redirect', iframeState.path)" -- web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx` returns exactly introducer 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 and remover/fix 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e. `git log -L 51,56:web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/UI/index.tsx 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e^` traces the redirect sink to 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 and shows 04aa5d9ad0506751b305cf86d18a8ca07358a906 changed only `visualEditing.enableDraftModeUrl` to `currentVisualEditing.enableDraftModeUrl`; `git blame -L '/new URLSearchParams(ctx.location.search)/',+4 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e^ -- web-previews/src/entrypoints/Inspector/ContentLinkContext/index.tsx` attributes the attacker-controlled `path` read to 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672. `git diff --name-status d42b0fc4e54d2e9731030812d2b98098cc6d1a95 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672 --` for the two Inspector files reports both as `A`, directly proving the immediate parent has neither vulnerable source nor sink. `git show 7965eebf0973cc5ebb18bc5ff9ce7ff19e89bb2e` adds `normalizePathForVisualEditing`: it resolves the candidate against `new URL(draftModeUrl).origin`, rejects a parsed origin that differs, emits only pathname/search/hash, applies safe fallbacks, and revalidates initialization, content-link state, navigation, frontend changes, and the final iframe redirect sink. The fix commit's package version remains 1.0.30; its immediate child a40b1e48bea2c352bb5c4838dbd536ee3c0457f0 is `Bump` and sets 1.0.31. The npm registry record `https://registry.npmjs.org/datocms-plugin-web-previews` maps 1.0.28 to gitHead 2eb2d7ef566844147123c3115221d8c1e0af3026 (published 2026-01-14; merge-base with the BIC is only parent d42b0fc4e54d2e9731030812d2b98098cc6d1a95), 1.0.29 to gitHead a933ee45d41b02d0d6643d8ebc1aa60f6929a993 (published 2026-01-26; its merge-base with the BIC is the BIC), 1.0.30 to branch head 3d697a3b3ebd280f36ae2a411199d2d715ca8b31 (published 2026-02-03), and fixed 1.0.31 to a40b1e48bea2c352bb5c4838dbd536ee3c0457f0 (published 2026-02-24). `git tag --contains` returns no repository tag for either BIC or fix, so the npm package gitHeads and package-version commits, rather than Git tags, establish the release boundary. Finally, `git cat-file -p 0fdfe73f8552e3fd5dcbc126ad9602346e3a1672` supplies the BIC-only marker check quoted in `ai_marker`.
reasoning: The security invariant is that iframe navigation must remain on the configured draft-mode frontend origin. The BIC simultaneously introduced the attacker-controlled inspector query input and the redirect-based iframe sink without validating that invariant. Its direct parent lacks both newly added Inspector files, while line history rejects the later frontend-selection edit and normal merge as origins. The advisory-linked fix closes the complete path by canonicalizing every path source and, critically, checking again at the redirect sink that `parsed.origin` equals the configured draft-mode origin; 1.0.31 is the immediate release bump containing that fix. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object. That object names a human author/committer and contains no AI/bot marker or trailer, so the correct closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any later commits or fix authorship.
